name: Landsat 9
primaryPayloads: Operational Land Imager 2 (OLI-2, 14-bit radiometric precision)
Thermal Infrared Sensor 2 (TIRS-2, dual-band split-window thermal radiometer)
keyDiscoveries: Over 50 years of uninterrupted continental environmental record continuation
Sub-field scale agricultural water evapotranspiration quantification
Immediate satellite tracking of severe global megafire boundary progression
lessonsLearned: Redundant split thermal channels overcome atmospheric water vapor contamination without requiring heavy active cooling on the optical bench.

name: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS)
primaryOrbit: P/2 Lunar-Resonant High Earth Orbit (108,000 x 375,000 km)
primaryPayloads: Four wide-field optical cameras (16.8 megapixel CCDs, combined 2,304 deg² FOV)
High-speed Ka-band phased array downlink transmitter
keyDiscoveries: Discovered over 7,000 candidate exoplanets and 400+ confirmed worlds
Discovered TOI-700 d, the first habitable-zone Earth-sized world found by TESS
Mapped full-sky stellar variability and asteroseismology on 200,000 bright stars
lessonsLearned: Selecting a lunar-resonant 13.7-day orbit eliminated thermal cycling and eclipse battery burdens, allowing an ultra-lightweight 362 kg smallsat to outperform multi-ton observatories.

name: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)
primaryOrbit: Sun-Earth L1 Halo Orbit (1.5 million km sunward)
primaryPayloads: LASCO (Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph C1/C2/C3)
EIT (Extreme Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope)
CELIAS (Charge, Element, and Isotope Analysis System)
keyDiscoveries: Revolutionized space weather forecasting by identifying halo CMEs aimed at Earth
Discovered over 5,000 sungrazing comets using automated coronagraph images
Mapped internal solar acoustic sound waves through helioseismology
lessonsLearned: Operating at L1 avoids Earth's magnetosphere and orbital day/night cycles, but attitude recovery after loss-of-signal requires robust gyroless momentum dump routines.

name: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
primaryOrbit: Sun-Earth L2 Halo Orbit (1.5 million km anti-sunward)
primaryPayloads: NIRCam (Near-Infrared Camera)
NIRSpec (Near-Infrared Spectrograph)
MIRI (Mid-Infrared Instrument with active pulse-tube cryocooler)
6.5-meter gold-coated beryllium primary mirror array
keyDiscoveries: Imaged earliest primordial galaxies formed within 300 million years of Big Bang
Detected CO2, water vapor, and methane in habitable-zone exoplanet atmospheres
Revealed proto-stellar disk star formation obscured by interstellar dust clouds
lessonsLearned: Deployable 5-layer Kapton sunshields passively cool telescope optics to 40K, reserving closed-cycle cryocoolers exclusively for long-wavelength mid-infrared detectors.

name: Tracking and Data Relay Satellite 13 (TDRS-M)
primaryPayloads: Dual 4.5-meter steerable carbon-composite parabolic reflector dishes
Multiple-Access phased array S-band / Ku-band / Ka-band transponders
High-power 3 kW GaAs solar array wings
keyDiscoveries: Maintained 99.9% continuous telemetry and 4K video for International Space Station
Enabled near-instantaneous global commanding of Hubble Space Telescope
Provided uninterrupted high-rate downlink pipelines for scientific launch vehicles
lessonsLearned: Stationing high-throughput transponders in geostationary orbit eliminates the need for expensive distributed networks of hundreds of terrestrial ground stations.

name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
primaryOrbit: Low Circular Lunar Polar Orbit (50 x 100 km, 90°)
primaryPayloads: LROC (Narrow Angle and Wide Angle High-Resolution Cameras)
LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter)
Diviner (Lunar Radiometer Experiment measuring sub-40K polar ice traps)
keyDiscoveries: Created the highest-resolution digital elevation model of any planetary body
Confirmed presence of water ice inside permanently shadowed polar regions
Mapped Apollo landing sites, lander stages, and astronaut rover wheel tracks
lessonsLearned: Lunar mass concentrations (mascons) perturb orbits rapidly; choosing frozen orbital inclinations minimizes fuel required for repetitive altitude adjustments.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram Lander & Pragyan Rover)
primaryOrbit: Lunar South Pole Surface (69.37° S, 32.35° E, Shiv Shakti Point)
primaryPayloads: ChASTE (Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment probe)
ILSA (Instrument for Lunar Seismic Activity)
LP (Langmuir Probe plasma density sensor)
Hazard Detection and Avoidance Cameras (LPDC/LHDAC)
keyDiscoveries: First successful soft landing in the lunar high-latitude southern polar region
Measured steep vertical temperature gradient in lunar regolith (60°C on surface to -10°C at 8cm depth)
In-situ sulfur and iron detection via rover Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy
lessonsLearned: Four throttleable 800N bipropellant engines paired with real-time velocity cameras provide critical stability margin when landing on 15° crater slopes.

name: Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN (MAVEN)
primaryOrbit: Elliptical Mars Orbit (150 x 6,200 km, 75° inclination)
primaryPayloads: NGIMS (Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer)
SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer)
IUVS (Imaging Ultraviolet Spectrograph)
Electra UHF Mars rover telecommunications relay
keyDiscoveries: Quantified that solar wind stripping caused Mars to lose over 85% of its atmosphere
Direct measurement of auroral displays triggered by solar energetic proton storms
Relayed majority of science data return from Curiosity and Perseverance rovers
lessonsLearned: Aerobraking passes into the Martian upper exosphere provide essential atmospheric samples while simultaneously lowering apogee without consuming propellant.
